summary.problem: Stable installations of Gemini CLI were automatically updated to nightly build versions.
summary.root_cause: In .github/actions/publish-release/action.yml, npm publish uses the invalid --no-tag flag. NPM defaults to tagging releases as 'latest' when no valid tag option is specified. As a result, daily nightly builds overwrite the 'latest' dist-tag on npm, causing stable installations to resolve and update to nightly releases.
summary.context: The release workflow runs daily for nightly builds and passes npm-tag='nightly' to the publish-release action. However, because publish-release invokes 'npm publish --no-tag', npm automatically assigns the 'latest' tag to the published nightly package before tag-npm-release runs.

steps: Locate the npm publish execution steps for CORE, CLI, and A2A packages.
Replace the invalid --no-tag flag in npm publish with --tag="${{ inputs.npm-tag }}".
Verify that npm publish correctly assigns the target distribution tag (such as nightly, preview, or latest) during package publication.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When publishing nightly or preview builds, npm publish tags the packages with the specified npm-tag (e.g., nightly) instead of defaulting to latest, ensuring stable installations on the latest dist-tag are unaffected.
verification_steps: Run a dry-run of the release action or inspect workflow steps to ensure 'npm publish --tag=${{ inputs.npm-tag }}' is invoked.
Verify npm dist-tag latest remains pointing to stable release versions and is not overwritten by nightly publications.

github_metadata.title: Stable installation was automatically updated to a nightly build
